faqs.q: What is the minimum wage in NSW for 2026-27?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage applies across Australia, including NSW, at $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. For a 38-hour week, that's $1,004.90 per week or $52,293 per year. Casual employees receive $33.05 per hour including 25% loading.

faqs.q: How do I convert hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by hours per week (usually 38) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,293. This assumes no unpaid overtime or penalty rates.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the minimum wage?

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Minimum Wage in NSW

If you are wondering what is minimum wage in NSW, the answer starts with the National Minimum Wage set by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026, the national rate is $26.44 per hour for a full-time employee working 38 hours per week. That works out to $1,004.90 per week and $52,293 per year before tax and super. This rate applies across all states and territories, including New South Wales. However, many employees are covered by awards or enterprise agreements that set higher minimum rates for specific industries or roles.

### The Basic Conversion Formula

To convert any hourly rate to an annual figure, use the simple formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the calculation is straightforward. For example, if you earn $30 per hour, your annual gross pay is $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. This formula assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It is a useful starting point for comparing job offers or understanding your total earnings.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many Australian employers pay wages fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by two. Using the minimum wage example: $1,004.90 per week becomes $2,009.80 per fortnight. This can help with budgeting and understanding your regular cash flow. The [the timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and see the corresponding weekly, fortnightly, and annual amounts instantly.

## Distinguishing Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

It is important to know that the National Minimum Wage is the legal floor. Most employees in NSW are covered by a modern award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or occupation. For instance, hospitality, retail, and construction awards each have specific pay rates. You can check your award on the Fair Work Ombudsman website or refer to the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for more details.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave entitlements. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). When using [the timesheet](/) on this site, you can tick a checkbox to add 25% casual loading to your base rate. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading; always start with the base hourly rate.

## Tax and Medicare Levy on Your Annual Pay

Once you have your annual gross figure, you need to estimate tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 income year, the resident tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

In addition, most residents pay a Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income. For a minimum wage earner on $52,293, the tax would be approximately $5,342 (using the 2026–27 scale) plus Medicare levy of $1,046, leaving an after-tax income of about $45,905. This is a rough estimate; your actual tax may vary based on deductions, offsets, and other factors. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page provides more detail on net income calculations.

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Superannuation guarantee contributions are not deducted from your wage; they are paid by your employer on top of your gross earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a minimum wage earner, that adds about $6,275 per year to your retirement savings. You can explore [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more information on salary sacrifice and contribution caps.

## NSW Average Earnings for Context

While the minimum wage is the legal floor, average earnings in NSW are higher. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, full-time adult ordinary time earnings in NSW were $2,108.80 per week as of May 2026. That is an average across all industries and occupations, not a median for any specific job. It gives context for where the minimum wage sits relative to the broader workforce. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page has more data from the ABS.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
